note: Per-theme fix candidates ranked most→least likely. Likelihood is heuristic, not a diagnosis.

disk-retries.symptom: Windows retried or failed I/O on a storage device

fixes.title: Bad cable, port, or USB hub power
fixes.why: Most portable SSD retries are interconnect — cable, front-panel hub, or weak power — not the NAND itself.
steps: Reseat the cable at both ends.
Move the drive to a rear motherboard USB 3.x or Thunderbolt port (avoid front hubs).
Try a different short, quality cable if you have one.

fixes.title: Drive media starting to fail
fixes.why: Repeated retries after cable/port changes often mean the drive or enclosure bridge is dying.
steps: Copy important data off immediately.
Check SMART / manufacturer tools if internal; for USB enclosures, test the bare drive if possible.

fixes.title: USB selective suspend / sleep power cut
fixes.why: Windows power management can spin down USB devices mid-transfer.
steps: Power Options → change plan → USB settings → disable selective suspend (test).
In Device Manager, USB Root Hubs → Power Management → uncheck 'allow computer to turn off this device' (test).

fixes.title: Storage / USB controller driver glitch
fixes.why: Less common; chipset or enclosure firmware mismatches.
steps: Install board chipset + USB drivers from the motherboard support page.
Update enclosure firmware if the vendor provides it.

ethernet-link.symptom: Wired network link drops and returns

fixes.title: Cable or switch/router port
fixes.why: Physical layer is the #1 cause of link flaps.
steps: Reseat Ethernet at PC and switch.
Try a known-good Cat5e/Cat6 cable and another switch port.

fixes.title: NIC power-saving turns the adapter off
fixes.why: Windows often allows the OS to power down the Ethernet adapter.
steps: Device Manager → Network adapters → your Ethernet → Power Management → uncheck allow turn off.

fixes.title: Outdated or buggy NIC driver
fixes.why: Intel I226 and similar need current drivers from the board vendor.
steps: Install LAN driver from ASUS (or board OEM) support — avoid random pack sites.

fixes.title: Failing NIC or motherboard LAN PHY
fixes.why: Rare; after cable/driver/power checks fail.
steps: Test a USB Ethernet adapter; if stable, board LAN may be failing.

usb-errors.symptom: USB device failed to start, reset, or was removed unexpectedly

fixes.title: Bluetooth stack conflict (onboard + dongle)
fixes.why: Very common on gaming boards with Intel Wi‑Fi/BT plus a USB BT dongle.
steps: Unplug USB BT dongle; reboot; use onboard only — or disable onboard BT and use the dongle alone.

fixes.title: Port power / USB hub overload
fixes.why: High-draw devices on front hubs or weak ports reset under load.
steps: Move device to rear motherboard USB port.
Remove unneeded USB devices; try without hubs.

fixes.title: Broken or ghost device driver
fixes.why: Leftover drivers after unplugging devices show as error codes.
steps: Use Ghost Device Cleaner for non-present devices.
In Device Manager, uninstall the failed device and rescan.

fixes.title: xHCI selective suspend / power management
fixes.why: Known class of USB disconnect issues on Windows.
steps: Disable USB selective suspend; review USB Root Hub power management.

gpu-watchdog.symptom: Display driver stopped responding and recovered (TDR)

fixes.title: GPU driver bug or corruption
fixes.why: Most TDR recoveries after game updates are driver-related.
steps: Clean-install current NVIDIA/AMD drivers (or DDU if comfortable).

fixes.title: Power limit, loose cable, or overheating
fixes.why: Undervoltage or thermal throttling can look like driver timeouts.
steps: Reseat GPU power connectors; check case airflow and GPU temps under load.

fixes.title: Unstable factory/manual overclock
fixes.why: GPU or memory OC past stability causes TDRs.
steps: Reset GPU OC / dual-BIOS to stock; test without Afterburner profiles.

fixes.title: Failing GPU VRAM / board
fixes.why: Last resort after drivers, power, and stock clocks.
steps: Test in another PC or under warranty RMA path if artifacts persist.

kernel-power-41.symptom: Unexpected reboot — Windows did not shut down cleanly

fixes.title: Wall power / PSU cut (you forced it or power failed)
fixes.why: Event 41 after a known outage or holding the power button is expected, not a bug.
steps: Match the timestamp to a power outage or manual hard reset you remember.
If explained, no hardware chase needed for that instance.

fixes.title: Hard hang (GPU, storage, or CPU freeze)
fixes.why: If the PC froze then rebooted without a clean BSOD log, look for GPU/disk themes nearby in time.
steps: Check Event Viewer for GPU TDR or disk errors minutes before the 41.
Run memory test if freezes continue with no other clues.

fixes.title: PSU or power delivery instability
fixes.why: Random 41s under load with no crash dump can be power.
steps: Note if it happens under high GPU+CPU load; test with lower power limits; PSU health check.

fixes.title: CPU power limits / BIOS stability (esp. 14th-gen Intel)
fixes.why: Aggressive motherboard power defaults contributed to instability on some platforms.
steps: Update BIOS; apply Intel default / recommended power profiles from board maker.

fixes.title: Usually safe to ignore (background clutter)
fixes.why: Hundreds of DCOM timeouts are extremely common and almost never the root of user-facing problems.
steps: Do nothing unless a specific app feature is broken.
If printing/scanning fails, focus on that app — not DCOM itself.

fixes.title: A specific service is hung
fixes.why: Rarely, one broken app floods DCOM.
steps: Note the app name in the message; repair/reinstall that app only.

brother-brlog.symptom: Brother printer software logging IP / feature noise

fixes.title: Ignore if printing works
fixes.why: BrLog spam is normal when the printer is offline or a cloud feature has no IP.
steps: Only dig if print/scan fails.

fixes.title: Printer offline or wrong network
fixes.why: Wi‑Fi printer not on same LAN.
steps: Power-cycle printer; rejoin Wi‑Fi; use USB temporarily.

fixes.title: Remove unused Brother suite
fixes.why: If you no longer own the printer, leftover software logs forever.
steps: Uninstall Brother software you do not need.

fixes.title: One-off during update or install
fixes.why: Services restart during Windows Update and app installs.
steps: If it was a single event after an update, watch only.

fixes.title: Third-party service crashing
fixes.why: Look at the service name in the message.
steps: Identify service → update or reinstall that product.

fixes.title: Dependency or permission problem
fixes.why: Service needs another service or account rights.
steps: services.msc → Dependencies; check Event message for the service name.

fixes.title: Routine update activity
fixes.why: Most Update Client events are normal progress.
steps: Only care if Settings → Windows Update shows a failed install.

fixes.title: Stuck update needs repair
fixes.why: Failed installs leave error codes.
steps: Retry update; run Windows Update Troubleshooter; free disk space.

fixes.title: Component store issues
fixes.why: Rare; DISM/SFC territory.
steps: Only after free space + retry fail: DISM / SFC from official docs.

fixes.title: Normal on ASUS / gaming boards
fixes.why: EC traffic is expected; almost never actionable.
steps: Ignore unless paired with actual power or fan failures.

fixes.title: BIOS update if fans/power misbehave
fixes.why: Only if real hardware symptoms exist.
steps: Update BIOS from board support page carefully.

fixes.title: One app with bad TLS or proxy
fixes.why: Usually isolated to a browser, VPN, or corporate proxy.
steps: Note the process if listed; update that app; check system time.

fixes.title: Wrong system clock
fixes.why: Certificates fail when the clock is wrong.
steps: Enable automatic time; set correct time zone.

fixes.title: Security product HTTPS inspection
fixes.why: Some AV products intercept TLS.
steps: Temporarily test with HTTPS scanning disabled if a site fails.

fixes.title: After installing/removing antivirus
fixes.why: Filter stack changes log noise.
steps: Reboot after AV install/uninstall; one AV product only.

fixes.title: Backup or sync client filter
fixes.why: OneDrive/backup agents attach filters.
steps: Update the backup/sync app if file access fails.

fixes.title: Harmless informational noise
fixes.why: No user symptom.
steps: Ignore if nothing is broken.

fixes.title: Read the raw provider + message
fixes.why: Unknown themes need the actual text — often an app name is in the message.
steps: Open the Deep Dive sample messages and search the provider online with your board name.

fixes.title: Correlate with what you were doing
fixes.why: Installers, games, and sleep/wake produce burst errors.
steps: Match timestamps to sleep, updates, or a specific app launch.

fixes.title: Single low-volume warning — watch only
fixes.why: One-off warnings are often noise.
steps: Only escalate if it repeats daily or you feel a real symptom.
